company.name: Nimbus Notes
company.description: A note-taking app for teams. Most new accounts start from the website's free trial button.

title: Nimbus Notes: the sign-up page
brief: This is the signup page of Nimbus Notes, as it ships today. Use it like a customer would, then mark every usability problem you find: click the part of the screen, name the problem and say what you saw. Some parts are fine, and flagging them counts against you.

issues.explanation: The title is the same size and weight as body text, and the subtitle comes before it, so nothing tells the eye where the page starts or what it is for.
issues.fix: Make the title the largest, boldest text on the page and put it first, with the subtitle below in a lighter style.

issues.explanation: The field names live only in the placeholders, which disappear as soon as you type. The password rules are not shown at all, so people find them out from an error.
issues.fix: Put a visible label above each field and show the password rules before the user types.

issues.explanation: The consent text is legal jargon ('accede', 'PII', 'Art. 6(1)(a)', 'sub-processors'). People tick it without understanding what they agree to, which helps neither them nor the company.
issues.fix: Say it in plain words ('I agree to the Terms and the Privacy Policy') and link to the details.

hidden.principle: Judge a screen by the user's goal: every element should help them reach it, say clearly what will happen, and tell them what did happen.

props.heading: Create your Nimbus Notes account
props.subtitle: Start your 14-day free trial. No credit card needed.

props.text: By proceeding you accede to the processing of PII pursuant to Art. 6(1)(a) and the DPA, incl. onward transfers to sub-processors.

props.secondary: Already have an account? Log in
props.onSubmit: Check your inbox: we sent you a link to confirm your email.

props.text: Your trial ends after 14 days. We will remind you 3 days before, and nothing is charged unless you choose a plan.

userGoal: A visitor who clicked 'Start free trial' on the Nimbus Notes website wants to create an account and get into the product.
